source: Build a rooftop battle arena for a tagging game. The rooftop floor should be a large flat surface. Include multiple objects that players can use as cover and obstacles during a tag/chase game: - Several AC units / air conditioning boxes of varying sizes scattered around the floor - A few low walls / parapet walls around the edges that act as railings and barriers - A couple of elevated platforms at different heights for vantage points - Some ramps connecting different height levels so players can run up and down - A few stacked crates / boxes for hiding and dodging - A small rooftop shed/penthouse structure that players can run around Make it feel like an urban building rooftop. Expose configurable attributes for: floor size, wall height, number of AC units, crate count, and platform height so the user can adjust the arena layout. Keep it blocky and stylized with materials like concrete and metal.
scene_prompt: Build a blocky, stylized urban building rooftop arena. A large flat concrete rooftop floor forms the main play area, enclosed by low parapet walls around its edges. Scatter several metal air-conditioning units of varying sizes and stacked crates across the floor as cover, with a small rooftop shed or penthouse structure positioned so players can run around it. Place a couple of elevated platforms at different heights, connected to the main roof and each other by ramps, creating vertical vantage points and routes. Use concrete and metal materials throughout; make the floor size, wall height, AC-unit count, crate count, and platform heights adjustable layout dimensions.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Party & Casual: this is a tag/chase game in one shared arena. There is no secondary genre.

### Shape and preset
Use `arena-tiered`, taken from outside Party & Casual’s usual shape set, because the otherwise flat rooftop includes raised platforms joined by ramps without stacked or overhanging floors. The closest Party & Casual preset is Childhood Game, but use none: its maze and lobby are not present, while this scene’s vertical rooftop geometry overrides its bounded-flat shape.

### Config requirements
Use `cover-los` for scattered cover and sightline breaks: several varied metal AC units, a few stacks of crates, the rooftop shed, and the raised platforms all provide hiding and dodging geometry. The low parapet walls are the visible perimeter and edge barriers of the roof, but do not imply a lethal drop.

### Layout requirements
Use `spawn-protected` with evenly distributed round-start markers in separated, screened positions around the main roof, not directly exposed across the open floor. Use `trigger-scoring` as a tag-registration volume covering the active rooftop floor, excluding the exterior beyond the parapets and inaccessible shed roof geometry.

### Layout components
The single main zone is a large, adjustable flat concrete rooftop, occupying most of the frame. A small penthouse or rooftop shed sits off-centre so it can be circled on both sides. Several adjustable-count AC units of varying footprint and height are scattered in loose cover clusters; a few adjustable-count stacked-crate groups fill remaining dodge routes without sealing them. A couple of elevated metal-and-concrete platforms at distinct adjustable heights sit on different sides of the roof, with broad ramps connecting each platform to the main floor and giving continuous run-up routes. Low adjustable-height parapet walls trace the full roof boundary, interrupted only where ramps and circulation require clearance. Keep open lanes between cover clusters for chasing. Frame the whole roof in an isometric three-quarter view, with the parapet outline, shed, ramps, and both platforms all legible.

### Render order
Use `isometric`: the arena remains playable if cover spacing is visually approximate, so a look-led rooftop composition is authoritative rather than a topology-first plan.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium, driven by one large roof with several cover clusters and two elevated route areas. Theme: blocky stylized urban rooftop, concrete slabs, galvanized metal, industrial AC housings, and muted city-building detail. Use `tiered` because the ramps and raised platforms create real non-overhanging elevation; no other pipeline modifier is forced.
